1. What it is.text: Mercury is a fintech, not a bank. Your deposits sit at Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., and Patriot Bank issues its IO charge card. Founded in 2017, it raised a $200M Series D at a $5.2B valuation in May 2026 and says more than 300,000 customers use it. 1. What it is.research_text: Mercury is a fintech, not a bank. Its own footer reads "Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank" and names Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC, as the banks providing the accounts (pricing page, read 5 October 2026). Those two banks hold your deposits; Mercury's partner-bank page also lists Patriot Bank, N.A., which issues the IO charge card. Column was added on 19 October 2024. Evolve Bank & Trust had been a partner since 2019; Mercury announced in March 2025 that it was moving customers off Evolve, with the rollover run in cohorts over months. Mercury Technologies, Inc. was founded in 2017, is venture-backed and is based in San Francisco. It raised a $200M Series D led by TCV at a $5.2B valuation on 20 May 2026, reported $650M annualized revenue as of Q3 2025 with four consecutive years of GAAP net income and EBITDA profitability, and says more than 300,000 customers use it (as of 20 May 2026). Charter status: the OCC granted preliminary conditional approval for Mercury Bank, N.A., Salt Lake City, Utah on 24 April 2026; that approval requires at least $300M of paid-in capital and expires if the bank has not opened within 18 months of that date. The FDIC approved deposit insurance on 8 September 2026, also conditional on at least $300M of capital and on all other final approvals, and that consent lapses after one year. Mercury Technologies still needs Federal Reserve approval as the bank holding company; trade press on 10 September 2026 said the bank is projected to open in 2027. Until it opens, deposits stay at the partner banks. The OCC decision states the new bank "anticipates transitioning customers from Mercury bank partners to the Bank" and will have no physical branches. The sources used here do not state total deposits held.

2. Eligibility & onboarding.text: Open to US-formed companies with US operations even if the founders live abroad. The FAQ (read 5 October 2026) allows a residential or international principal address but not a registered agent, P.O. box or UPS box, and excludes founders in listed countries; in July 2024 it closed accounts in Nigeria and other African countries. You upload formation documents, the EIN letter and a passport or other ID for owners of 25% or more; the FAQ does not say a passport fully replaces an SSN. No minimum, no branch, and 10 minutes or less to open.
2. Eligibility & onboarding.research_text: Mercury's FAQ (read 5 October 2026) says customers "must be formed and registered in the United States or a U.S. territory" and must "have some type of existing or planned operations in the U.S." The principal place of business can be a US or international address and can be residential, but "may not be a registered agent, P.O. box, or UPS box address". Founders can live outside the US: the FAQ says "we're proud to support U.S. companies founded by people across the globe", except where a founder or financial controller lives in a listed prohibited country. That list is enforced. In July 2024 Mercury told businesses in Nigeria and a dozen other African countries that accounts would close by 22 August 2024, and press at the time also named Ukraine, Croatia, Russia, Iran, Libya and North Korea, with Mercury saying "navigating current US sanctions programmes has become too complex". You upload formation documents, the IRS EIN letter and a government ID such as a passport for at least one person with operating control and for every owner holding 25% or more; the FAQ says an SSN is used "solely to verify your identity" and no credit check is run. The FAQ does not say whether a passport can fully replace an SSN, so that point is unverified. Money services businesses, adult entertainment, cannabis, internet gambling and trusts are excluded. There is no minimum balance to open and no branch visit; the FAQ says "Open your account in 10 minutes or less" (as of 5 October 2026). The sources used here do not state typical approval time or whether sole proprietors are accepted.

3. Fees & minimums.research_text: Three plans as of 5 October 2026: Mercury at $0 per month, Mercury Plus at $29.90 per month and Mercury Pro at $299 per month. Plus adds invoicing with ACH debit at $1 per transaction, recurring invoices, unlimited 1099 filings and six months of free Xero; Pro adds a relationship manager, $0 ACH-debit invoicing and NetSuite categorizations. Non-USD debit card purchases carry a currency exchange fee of up to 3%, and the IO card agreement (last updated 10 August 2026) sets its foreign transaction fee at 3.00%. USD card transactions are free. Cash deposits are not accepted. Checks: up to six free checkbooks a year and $0 to mail a check. The Column account agreement (updated 14 August 2026) lists a $15 fee for a principal-protected international wire and no closure or dormancy fee. 1099 filings cost $5 per form on the free plan. Mercury Books bookkeeping is $35 per month, waived until 31 December 2026. Mercury Personal ($240 per year) is included with a business account. Card payments on invoices run through Stripe at typically 2.9% + $0.30. ATM withdrawals carry no Mercury fee beyond the operator's charge. The pages that opened do not state wire or ACH limits.

4. Yield & treasury.research_text: Checking and savings pay nothing. The Column N.A. deposit agreement (updated 14 August 2026) lists a checking APY of 0.00% and a savings rate of 0.001% (0.00% APY). Yield comes only from Mercury Treasury, run by Mercury Advisory, LLC, an SEC-registered adviser, with Apex Clearing as broker. It needs a minimum of $250,000 across all Mercury accounts (as of 5 October 2026). The headline "up to 4.00%" is, in the page's own words, "for Mercury deposit sizes over $20M". The published net tiers as of 2 October 2026 are 3.15% in the government money market fund MRGXX or 3.55% in the ultra-short bond fund MCRYX for $250K to $2M, rising to 3.60% or 4.00% at $20M to $50M. The fee is 0.15% to 0.6% a year, set by total Mercury deposits, and quoted yields are net of that fee. Mercury announced the two Mercury-class funds on 18 August 2026: Morgan Stanley's MCRYX with 1 to 2 day liquidity, available at launch, and State Street's MRGXX with same-day liquidity, which the post said would arrive the following week. Note one inconsistency: the Treasury disclosures say MCRYX applies only to clients with $20M or more, while the Treasury page's tier table lists MCRYX yields from $250K, so confirm which fund you are offered. Treasury balances "are not FDIC insured, are not bank deposits" and "may lose value"; SIPC covers $500,000 of securities and cash with a $250,000 cash cap. Mercury Personal pays 3.50% APY on personal savings (page read 5 October 2026, no as-of date shown), but that is a consumer account, not the business account. The sources used here do not state any promotional business savings rate.

5. FDIC coverage & safety.text: Up to $5M of FDIC coverage on the free plan comes from sweeping deposits across up to 20 banks. It is pass-through insurance: it pays if an insured bank fails, not if Mercury fails, and Treasury balances are not covered. An industry tracker lists Choice Financial Group under an FDIC consent order dated December 2023, and former partner Evolve Bank & Trust received a Federal Reserve order in June 2024. Freeze and closure reports recur: 21% of 2,839 Trustpilot reviews are one-star (5 October 2026).
5. FDIC coverage & safety.research_text: Deposits sit at Choice Financial Group and Column N.A. The FAQ (read 5 October 2026) promises "up to $5M in FDIC insurance through our partner banks and their sweep networks" by "automatically spreading your deposits across up to 20 different banks". Column publishes the list of banks in its sweep network (revised 17 December 2024). This is pass-through coverage: it pays if an insured program bank fails, not if Mercury fails, as the footer line "Deposit insurance covers the failure of an insured bank" makes clear. Treasury balances are not FDIC insured. The sources used here do not state whether any Mercury customers lost access to funds in the 2024 Synapse collapse. Mercury's then-partner Evolve Bank & Trust received a Federal Reserve enforcement action on 14 June 2024 for lacking "an effective risk management framework" for its fintech partnerships, and Mercury announced its exit from Evolve in March 2025. An industry tracker dated 3 September 2026 lists Choice Financial Group under joint FDIC and North Dakota Consent Order FDIC-23-0086b dated 18 December 2023 as still in effect; the order text itself did not open, so this rests on the tracker. The Column agreement (14 August 2026) lets the bank "cancel or suspend your Accounts ... at any time" and place holds without prior notice, returning balances by ACH or paper check. Freeze and closure complaints are frequent: Trustpilot shows 2,839 reviews with a star breakdown of 21% one-star (read 5 October 2026), the newest, dated 2 October 2026, describing a closure with more than $100K held for 60 days, and a 30 May 2025 Hacker News thread includes a founder reporting a $250,000 incoming wire lost for a week.

6. Cards, credit & spend controls.text: The IO card is a charge card from Patriot Bank with no personal guarantee. It has no annual fee, no late fee and unlimited 1.5% cashback; you repay daily until balances reach $15K, then can switch to 30-day terms, and non-USD spend costs 3.00%. Admins get virtual cards, per-person limits and merchant-locked cards. Venture debt from Mercury Lending is for companies that raised venture capital in the last 12 months, and is not offered in California.
6. Cards, credit & spend controls.research_text: Debit cards are Mastercards issued by Choice Financial Group and Column N.A. (business disclosures, read 5 October 2026), with no Mercury fee at ATMs beyond the operator's charge and a currency exchange fee of up to 3% on non-USD purchases. The IO card is a charge card, not a revolving line: the credit page says it "requires the full balance to be paid each month". It is issued by Patriot Bank, N.A. on Mastercard, pays unlimited 1.5% cashback, and has no annual fee, no late fee and no personal guarantee (credit page read 5 October 2026; card agreement last updated 10 August 2026). New customers with lower balances start on daily repayment; once balances reach $15K you can switch to 30-day terms. The limit is based on the total balances you hold with Mercury plus any linked external accounts; the sources used here do not state a formula, a cap or a minimum balance to get the card. Non-USD IO transactions carry a 3.00% foreign transaction fee. Virtual cards are available on approval, and admins can set daily, weekly or monthly limits per team member, custom card expiration dates and cards locked to specific merchants. Mercury Spend (announced 11 August 2026) adds budgets, stipends, Gmail receipt scanning, reimbursements and policy settings that lock cards with overdue tasks. The Column deposit agreement (updated 14 August 2026) says that after closure "we will return the remaining balances to you via ACH transfer to one of your external accounts on Bank's records or via paper check to the address on file"; it lists no closure or dormancy fee. Statements download from the Documents tab, CSV downloads are available for accounting, and the API returns transaction history, so you can take your data with you. The larger risk is partner-bank changes that alter your routing details. Mercury moved customers off Evolve after its March 2025 announcement "in cohorts over a period of months". The OCC decision of 24 April 2026 states the planned Mercury Bank, N.A. "anticipates transitioning customers from Mercury bank partners to the Bank", and that approval expires if the bank has not opened within 18 months of that date; trade press (10 September 2026) projects opening in 2027. Mercury said on 19 December 2025 that "for customers, nothing changes today". Switching in gets an implementation team to map your setup and move funds, and you can keep your existing bank active during the move. The sources used here do not state a bulk vendor-import tool, whether account numbers survive the charter transition, or how long closed-account funds take to arrive; the newest Trustpilot review (2 October 2026) reports a 60-day hold after closure.

2. Eligibility & onboarding.research_text: You need a US-registered C-corp, S-corp, LLC or LLP with a US EIN, US operations and a US physical address; USPS PO boxes, private mailboxes and mailbox services are refused. If the business address is a virtual registration address with no physical presence, the beneficial owner or control officer must maintain a physical presence and be verifiable in the US, and Brex may ask for a utility bill or bank statement issued within the last three months or a lease issued within the past two years. Owners of 25% or more, control officers and the people who will transact give full legal name, date of birth, a residential or business street address and a taxpayer ID; those without an SSN can give a passport number and country of issuance, or a driver's license number. Brex's global-founders post (published 13 October 2021, modified 29 February 2024) says founders abroad can apply with a US incorporation, EIN, billing address and operations. A Trustpilot reviewer on 26 May 2026, after four years as a customer, reports Brex now accepts only customers with a US company and a US residential address; treat that as a user report, since no official page says it. Minimums: the monthly-payments card needs $50,000 cash for funded startups (lower via some partner referrals); unfunded companies can still apply and may be offered the daily-payments product. No minimum is stated for the checking account itself. Documents: unexpired photo ID (passport, US driver's license or state ID), EIN letter (CP 575 or 147-C), formation documents, and bank statements or a bank connection. Brex says the account opens in minutes (as of 5 October 2026); the sources used here do not state typical approval time.

4. Yield & treasury.research_text: Checking pays nothing: the fee schedule lists uninvested cash as "No yield" as of 5 October 2026. Yield comes from Treasury, where money buys shares of the BNY Dreyfus Government Cash Management fund (DGVXX), a government money market fund held at Bank of New York Mellon through Brex Treasury LLC. As of 5 October 2026 Brex's page cites a DGVXX 7-day yield of 3.50% (the fund's own page shows 3.46% as of 2 October 2026), and the posted "total treasury return" (fund yield plus an extra return paid by Brex, annualized and compounded on the assumption that payouts are reinvested for a year) is 3.56% for total balances under $500K, 3.61% for $500K to $2M, 3.71% for $2M to $5M, 3.76% for $5M to $20M and 3.91% above $20M. Your tier is set daily on combined checking, Treasury and Vault balances, but the extra return is paid only on Treasury funds, calculated daily and paid monthly. There is no minimum deposit. Transfers between checking and Treasury process in as little as one hour between 8 am and 3 pm ET on business days; Vault moves take 1 to 2 business days; neither Treasury nor Vault can send or receive outside payments. Treasury holdings are securities, not deposits: they are not FDIC insured and are covered by SIPC up to $500,000 including $250,000 in cash. 6. Cards, credit & spend controls.research_text: Brex cards are Visa or Mastercard cards issued by Emigrant Bank, Fifth Third Bank, N.A., or another bank named on the back of the card, not by Brex. Two payment models exist. Daily payments: the spending limit tracks your available Brex business account balance and payments are withdrawn the business day after a transaction clears. Monthly payments: a card with a 30-day statement period whose balance is withdrawn from your Brex account or linked account; funded startups need $50,000 in cash. Brex requires no personal guarantee and sets limits on revenue, amount raised or cash balance rather than a personal credit score; it advertises limits up to 30x higher than traditional business credit cards as of 5 October 2026 without giving a base figure. Points on the monthly card: 7x rideshare, 4x Brex-booked travel, 3x restaurants, 2x recurring software, 1x everything else; the daily-payments software variant pays 8x, 5x, 4x and 3x. Redemption as of 5 October 2026 is 0.6 cents per point for cash or statement credit and 1 cent for Brex travel, so 1x spend returns 0.6% in cash. Controls: unlimited virtual cards with limits by category, merchant and amount, and AI-powered custom rules on the $0 Essentials plan; multiple customizable expense policies and live budgets need Premium at $12 per user per month (as of 5 October 2026). Late payments cost 2.99% of the delinquent balance or $38, whichever is higher, and foreign card spend carries up to a 3% FX markup. A Trustpilot review on 19 May 2026 reports a limit cut to zero overnight. The sources used here do not describe a venture debt or line-of-credit product.

2. Eligibility & onboarding.research_text: Rho accepts US-incorporated entities only. Its help center says entities "must be incorporated in the United States, and either hold a US Operating Address or have one business owner based in the United States with a valid tax identification number (SSN)" (no date shown; fetched 5 October 2026). Rho's own guide (updated 5 October 2026) states it needs "at least one US-based owner or officer and a physical US operating address" and that "Rho verifies founders without an SSN or TIN by passport". A founder living abroad can be on the cap table, but a company with no US-based owner or officer and no US operating address does not qualify. The sources used here do not state whether a registered-agent or virtual-office address counts as an operating address. Sole proprietors are not accepted (NerdWallet, 7 January 2026); a single-member LLC "banking purely on an SSN, with no EIN in process, isn't a fit for Rho today" (Rho, 5 October 2026). Documents: EIN, formation papers, ownership details for owners of 25% or more, and government photo ID; Rho says "The application takes less than 10 minutes" (product page, fetched 5 October 2026). There is no minimum balance to open. Rho also incorporates companies: a Delaware C-corp for $400 or an LLC for $349, with the account opening in the same flow before the EIN arrives, though "funds cannot move until the IRS issues your EIN" (as of 5 October 2026). Residents of eight sanctioned countries are excluded (fetched 5 October 2026). Rho's terms let it close accounts "at any time for no reason or for any reason without prior notice" (terms dated 27 August 2026), and Trustpilot reviews dated October 2025 to August 2026 describe post-opening document requests and declined applications.

5. FDIC coverage & safety.research_text: Two different mechanisms apply. Checking: deposits sit at Webster Bank, a division of Santander Bank, N.A., or Lead Bank, and are insured up to $250,000 per customer "across all Rho checking accounts", not per sub-account (help center, fetched 5 October 2026). Savings: a sweep administered by American Deposit Management spreads balances "in increments below the $250,000 per-bank FDIC limit" across "400+ FDIC- and NCUA-insured institutions (as of August 2026)" for up to $75 million of coverage (help center, August 2026). Rho Treasury is not FDIC insured; it holds securities with SIPC protection up to $500,000 (treasury page, 5 October 2026). Rho states that FDIC insurance "does not protect you against the failure of Rho" (Rho blog, updated 5 October 2026). On partner-bank risk: Webster Bank, N.A. merged into Santander Bank, N.A. on 20 August 2026; Santander said accounts "can continue to be accessed and used in the same way" and "no action is required of customers at this time" (Santander, 20 August 2026). The sources used here do not record any losses for Rho customers in the 2023-2024 bank and BaaS failures, and no regulator action against Rho was found. On freezes: Rho's terms (27 August 2026) let it suspend or close accounts without notice. Trustpilot reviews dated November 2025 ($300,000 held "for weeks without any explanation") and October 2025 (closure after a document request) describe holds, and the site's 53 reviews score 3.4 out of 5 with 26% one-star (fetched 5 October 2026). International payments pass sanctions and AML screening; "Most reviews clear within a few business days" with no promised timeline (fetched 5 October 2026).

6. Cards, credit & spend controls.research_text: The Rho Corporate Card is a Mastercard World Elite Business charge card issued by Lead Bank or Webster Bank, a division of Santander Bank, N.A. (cards page, competitive data as of 8 September 2026); the full statement balance is paid each period, so it does not revolve. Two repayment modes exist. Every account starts on Daily Terms, where spend is repaid the following day from Rho Checking. Monthly Terms is "A 30-day billing cycle with a 1-day repayment period", available once you hold $25,000 at Rho or $75,000 combined with linked external accounts and pass underwriting (help center and product page, fetched 5 October 2026). Rho says "No personal guarantee, no consumer credit report, no personal credit score pull" and that it does not report business card activity to personal credit bureaus (fetched 5 October 2026). Cashback as of 5 October 2026: 1.25% on Daily Terms and 1% on Monthly Terms, rising to up to 2% and 1.75% with Rho Platinum, on up to $1,000,000 of eligible spend per calendar year. Rewards must be redeemed within twelve months or are forfeited, and "Transactions conducted or authorized in non-U.S. jurisdictions", utilities, money transfers and Walmart are excluded (rewards terms dated 10 April 2025). The sources used here do not state a foreign transaction fee on the card. Controls (help center, fetched 5 October 2026): virtual cards issued in seconds, limits that are fixed, single-use or recurring from daily to annual, Mastercard merchant-category locks, a lock to up to 20 named merchants, active date windows, vendor cards, and fixed cards that lock once transactions settle. Credit: Rho Capital is "a revolving line against your business cash flow, not a term loan or a venture-debt facility", with loans made by Lead Bank, up to $5 million, up to 180 days to repay each draw and a $0 prepayment penalty (product page, fetched 5 October 2026). Unlike the card, Capital requires "consent to obtain personal credit report", is "Subject to minimum revenue and business requirements", may need a personal guaranty, and is underwritten with Slope, a fintech (same page). No venture debt product is offered.

7. Payments & international.research_text: Domestic payments are free as of 5 October 2026: same-day ACH, standard ACH, domestic wires and mailed checks all cost $0, and Rho's help center says "Rho does not charge for sending and receiving ACHs or wires" (fetched 5 October 2026). Timing (help center, fetched 5 October 2026): ACH created before 2 pm ET and under $1 million settles the same day, otherwise next day; domestic wires before 4:45 pm ET arrive the same day; internal book transfers land within an hour; mailed checks take up to 8 business days by USPS and void after 90 days; remote check deposits clear in 2 to 3 business days, up to 6 to 7 under risk review, with deposits over $15,000 in a day subject to extra screening. Limits (fetched 5 October 2026): ACH pull $20 million a day and $10 million per transaction, ACH push $20 million a day, domestic wires out $90 million a day, international wires out $2.5 million a day, incoming international up to $10 million a day; larger amounts need advance notice. International payments run through Wise US Inc. to "over 200 countries and territories" in 23 listed currency codes including USD, EUR, GBP, INR, JPY, CAD and AUD (help center, fetched 5 October 2026). USD international wires carry no Rho fee; non-USD transfers pay a 1% conversion fee; an optional $15 flat fee covers SWIFT and intermediary charges; recalls cost $30 (5 October 2026). Delivery is 1 to 5 business days. Eight countries are blocked for all payments and 52 more are restricted for bank payments, including Nigeria, Pakistan and Ukraine (the last two with exceptions for certain payments to individuals); crypto, gambling and weapons businesses cannot send international payments (fetched 5 October 2026). Approvals: scheduled payments go out around 4 am ET on the due date and any needing approval must be approved before then; bulk payments load from a Rho CSV template (fetched 5 October 2026). The sources used here do not mention RTP or FedNow instant payments.

8. Integrations & accounting.research_text: Native accounting integrations cover NetSuite, QuickBooks Online, Sage Intacct and Puzzle; Xero and QuickBooks Online can also connect by bank feed (help center, fetched 5 October 2026). The integrations page also lists Campfire, and the help center links a Rillet guide. QuickBooks syncing is a manual button press by default, with optional recurring syncs (fetched 5 October 2026). HR and payroll listings are BambooHR, Workday and Gusto; travel and expense listings are Navan, Emburse and SAP Concur (fetched 5 October 2026). The sources used here do not list Stripe or Rippling integrations. API: Rho offers a REST API with an OpenAPI spec at docs.rho.co covering accounts, transactions, statements, cards, invoicing, cash flow insights, users, reimbursements and credit, with rate limits documented. It is read-only: "Tokens are read-only and cannot initiate payments or modify accounts", webhooks are "Not yet" available, and "Write endpoints and webhooks are planned but are not currently available" (Rho, updated 5 October 2026). Tokens are created by an Account Owner or Admin, carry a required expiry of at most one year, expire after 45 days of inactivity, support optional IP allowlists and are capped at 20 active tokens per business; the API is "Available to every Rho customer, with no waitlist and no approval step" and carries no separate fee (5 October 2026). Rho also runs a read-only MCP server (docs.rho.co and product page, 5 October 2026). Sub-accounts: you can create multiple operating accounts under one entity; the sources used here do not state a cap. Accountant access: an External Accountant role gives reconciliation access "without the ability to take action on the account", an Investor role is "predominantly 'view only'", and a Bookkeeper role is "unable to view account balances or Vendor history" (help center, fetched 5 October 2026). Statements download from Settings and transactions export as CSV from the Banking tab (fetched 5 October 2026).

9. Lock-in & migration.research_text: Leaving is a support request, not a self-serve button. The closure article (fetched 5 October 2026) says "Closure must be requested by the Account Owner" by phone, chat or email; you must first settle any card balance, cancel scheduled payments, move Savings to Checking (typically next business day if created before 1 pm ET) and sell any Treasury holdings (typically 2 to 3 business days, at market price). Download statements and the CSV transaction export before closing, because "Your dashboard access ends when the account closes". The remaining balance is returned by wire or check. No closure fee appears in the article or in the terms dated 27 August 2026. Data portability is limited to statement PDFs, CSV exports and the read-only API; the sources used here do not describe a bulk vendor or bill export. Partner-bank change risk is real but has so far been quiet: Webster Bank, N.A. merged into Santander Bank, N.A. on 20 August 2026, Santander said accounts continue unchanged, and Rho's pages relabel the bank as "a division of Santander Bank, N.A." as of 5 October 2026. The sources used here do not state whether routing or account numbers would change if Rho moved to another partner bank. Coming in is easier: Rho Switch reads 120 days of activity through Plaid or uploaded statements and updates some payees automatically, and Rho says "Most customers complete the switching process in under 15 minutes" (help center, fetched 5 October 2026). Rho Platinum's rule that 50% or more of company assets sit at Rho (fetched 5 October 2026) means the top cashback rate disappears once you move cash elsewhere, which is the main soft lock-in.

12. Limitations.research_text: Eligibility is narrow: no sole proprietors (NerdWallet, 7 January 2026), no companies without a US-based owner or officer plus a physical US operating address (Rho, 5 October 2026), and no cash deposits or ATM access (NerdWallet, 7 January 2026). Savings yield is low at "up to 1.00%" as of 17 August 2026, needs $25,000 and allows six transfers out a month (August 2026); higher yield requires Treasury with its $50,000 minimum and 0.60% fee under $2 million (5 October 2026). Checking FDIC coverage is $250,000 in total across sub-accounts (5 October 2026). The card is charge-only, Monthly Terms needs $25,000 at Rho (5 October 2026), and non-US card transactions earn no cashback (rewards terms, 10 April 2025); the sources used here do not state a foreign transaction fee. Rho Capital, unlike the card, requires consent to a personal credit report (5 October 2026). International coverage lists 23 currencies and restricts 52 extra countries for bank payments (5 October 2026). No RTP or FedNow is documented. The API cannot send payments and has no webhooks (5 October 2026). Treasury's headline "Up to 4.57% net yield" on the homepage (14 August 2026) sits above the 4.00% top-tier figure on the treasury page (5 October 2026), so marketing and live rates differ. Trust signals are mixed: a 3.4 Trustpilot score from 53 reviews with 26% one-star (fetched 5 October 2026), including a $300,000 hold reported in November 2025, and terms that permit closure "without prior notice" (27 August 2026). Rho has no bank charter, and one of its two partner banks changed owners on 20 August 2026.

1. What it is.text: Relay is a financial technology company, not a bank. Deposits sit at Thread Bank, an FDIC-insured community bank in Tennessee that also issues the Relay Visa cards. Relay runs the app, the multi-account structure and integrations. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Toronto under co-founder and CEO Yoseph West, it took $50 million from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund in May 2026 after a $32.2 million Series B in May 2024, and reported more than 150,000 customers and $1.3 billion in deposits at that date.
1. What it is.research_text:
Relay is a financial technology company, not a bank. Its help center says "Relay is a financial technology company and is not an FDIC-insured bank" (updated 11 August 2026). Deposits sit at Thread Bank, an FDIC-insured community bank headquartered in Rogersville, Tennessee, chartered under Tennessee law and captioned by the FDIC as an insured state nonmember bank. Thread Bank holds the deposits, issues the Relay Visa debit and credit cards, and clears ACH, wires and check deposits; Relay runs the app, the multi-account structure, integrations and team permissions. The program partner named in the deposit agreement is Relay Financial Technologies Inc. (agreement last updated 1 September 2026). Relay Capital term loans are a separate product provided in partnership with Fundbox and its originating bank partner, Lead Bank, not Thread Bank (press report, 20 May 2026).

Relay is privately held and venture-backed. It was founded in 2018, is headquartered in Toronto, is led by co-founder and CEO Yoseph West, and had about 250 staff as of 20 May 2026. Investors named on its site include Bain Capital Ventures, Better Tomorrow Ventures and Garage Capital. General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund invested $50 million on 19 May 2026, after a $32.2 million Series B in May 2024. Scale as of 19 May 2026: more than 150,000 small business customers and more than $1.3 billion in managed deposits through Thread Bank. Relay says it is on track to reach 3.2 times its Series B revenue by the end of 2026; it does not disclose revenue or profitability.

2. Eligibility & onboarding.text: Relay opens accounts for US-registered LLCs and corporations as well as general partnerships and sole proprietorships. Corporations can be C corp or S corp; nothing registered outside the United States qualifies. The business address must be physical, with no PO boxes or virtual mailboxes. Founders abroad are accepted when the business has an operating presence in the US, but every beneficial owner must give a physical US address, and the two onboarding pages disagree on whether a passport number can replace an SSN (both updated August 2026). 2. Eligibility & onboarding.research_text:
Relay opens accounts for US-registered LLCs, corporations (C corp or S corp), general partnerships and sole proprietorships. It does not open personal, escrow, trust or retirement accounts, or accounts for businesses not registered in the United States (help center, updated 11 August 2026). Prohibited industries include cannabis and CBD, cryptocurrency, debt collection, direct marketing and telemarketing, gambling, NFTs, payday lending and prescription drug sales. LLCs, corporations and general partnerships supply an EIN and formation documents (Articles of Organization, Certificate of Formation or Articles of Incorporation); "Relay cannot support sole proprietors without a valid SSN or a physical U.S. address." The business address must be physical, "no PO boxes, no virtual mailboxes"; if the legal address is a registered agent, you also supply an operational address where business activity occurs, and that address cannot be another registered agent.

Founders outside the US: Relay "accepts U.S.-registered businesses owned by non-U.S. citizens or residents, provided the business has an operating presence in the U.S." Each beneficial owner gives a "Social Security Number (SSN) or passport number" and a "Physical U.S. address (no PO boxes, no virtual mailboxes)". Identity verification accepts a US driver's licence or "a valid passport (for non-US citizens)" plus a selfie and liveness check. A separate onboarding page says "every beneficial owner must have a valid SSN" (both updated 11 August 2026); the two pages conflict and the sources used here do not resolve it. Owners in 31 prohibited countries, including Nigeria, Pakistan, Russia and Ukraine, cannot be named on an application. The sources used here do not mention ITINs.

The application takes about 10 minutes online and "Most applications are reviewed within 1-2 business days"; missing information or extra screening takes longer. There is no minimum balance. The sources used here do not state a minimum opening deposit.

3. Fees & minimums.research_text:
Three plans, priced as of 17 September 2026: Starter $0 per month, Grow $30 per month, Scale $90 per month, marked "Discounted for a limited time" from a regular $120 (the deposit agreement dated 1 September 2026 lists Scale at $120). The pricing page states "No minimum balance. No hidden or overdraft fees." Starter and Grow allow up to 20 checking accounts, Scale up to 50; every plan allows up to two savings accounts and unlimited users. You can upgrade, downgrade or cancel at any time; "If you downgrade, the unused portion of the higher plan is credited back" (help center, updated 11 August 2026).

Per-transaction fees (help center, updated 11 August 2026, and deposit agreement, 1 September 2026): standard ACH free; same-day ACH $1 on Starter, $0.50 on Grow, free on Scale; outgoing domestic wire $8 / $5 / $5; outgoing SWIFT wire $25 / $22 / $20; outgoing Local Network international wire $5 / $3 / $1.50; stop payment $10; 1% on ATM or card transactions outside the US. The agreement lists an incoming wire fee of $5 on every tier, while the inbound international wire article says "Relay does not charge a fee to receive international wires", so confirm before relying on either figure. Collecting invoices costs 2.9% + $0.30 per card payment and 1% / 0.75% / 0.5% per pay-by-bank payment, deducted before deposit. Sending a paper check is free on all plans, and the mobile check deposit article states no fee. Cash deposits are free at Allpoint+ ATMs ($1,000 per transaction) and cost up to $4.95 at Green Dot retailers ($500 per transaction at most stores, $1,000 at Walmart, $1,500 per day). Closing the account costs nothing.

Yield & treasury.text: Only savings accounts earn interest, and the rate is a plan feature: 1.19% APY on Starter, 1.87% on Grow and 3.21% on Scale as of 17 September 2026, variable and paid monthly, with no minimum. Checking earns nothing. Because yield is bought with the subscription, Scale at $90 a month only beats Starter above roughly $53,500 of average savings balance. There is no treasury or money-market product: every balance is a bank deposit inside the FDIC sweep, so large idle cash that wants Treasury bill yield needs a separate brokerage account.
4. Yield & treasury.research_text:
Interest is paid only on savings accounts, and the rate depends on the plan. As of 17 September 2026 the savings APY is 1.19% on Starter, 1.87% on Grow and 3.21% on Scale (interest rates 1.18%, 1.86% and 3.16%). Relay states the rates "are variable and subject to change based on the target range of the Federal Funds rate". Interest is paid monthly, there is no minimum balance, and each business can open up to two savings accounts. The pricing page lists no APY for checking, and the sources used here do not state that checking earns anything.

Because the rate is a plan feature, the real cost of yield is the subscription. Scale at $90 per month is $1,080 a year; the 2.02 percentage-point gap over Starter pays for that only above roughly $53,500 of average savings balance (arithmetic on the 17 September 2026 rates, before the price reverts to $120). Grow at $30 per month ($360 a year) with a 0.68-point gap breaks even near $53,000.

The sources used here describe no treasury or money-market product. The pricing page, savings page and "What is Relay" article (updated 11 August 2026) describe only checking and savings, and none mentions a sweep into Treasury bills, a brokerage product or a management fee. Every balance is a bank deposit at Thread Bank and its program banks, so the FDIC sweep in factor 5 applies to it, up to $3,000,000. Founders holding large idle cash who want T-bill yield need a separate brokerage or treasury account.

5. FDIC coverage & safety.text: Deposits sit at Thread Bank, which uses IntraFi to spread balances above $250,000 across program banks for coverage up to $3,000,000. Each program bank holds up to $250,000, every customer is enrolled automatically, and the balance still shows as one number in the app. Thread Bank was under an FDIC consent order from May 2024 until the FDIC terminated it in December 2025. The deposit agreement lets the bank suspend or close your account with or without notice and pays out closed accounts by paper check. Trustpilot one-star reviews from July to September 2026 report closures without explanation and funds held for up to 45 days.
5. FDIC coverage & safety.research_text:
Relay is not a bank; deposits are held at Thread Bank, Member FDIC. Thread Bank uses IntraFi to place balances above $250,000 across a network of FDIC-insured program banks, each holding up to $250,000, for FDIC insurance coverage "up to $3,000,000" (help center, updated 11 August 2026). Every Relay customer is enrolled automatically, the program applies to Relay checking and savings accounts, the balance still shows as a single number in the app, and you transact from Relay as usual. "If your total deposits exceed $3,000,000, the excess sits at Truist Bank". The $250,000 at each program bank is "inclusive of any other deposits you may already hold at the bank in the same ownership capacity" (pricing page, 17 September 2026). The sources used here describe no treasury product, so there is no separate investment balance outside the sweep.

Regulator history: on 21 May 2024 the FDIC issued a consent order against Thread Bank requiring a documented risk assessment of its fintech partners and stronger customer due diligence, AML and beneficial-ownership controls in its banking-as-a-service program (press report, 18 December 2024). The FDIC terminated that order on 22 December 2025 (order FDIC-24-0022b, listed in the FDIC's December 2025 enforcement release dated 30 January 2026). The sources used here do not describe any effect on Relay customers from the 2023 to 2024 bank and BaaS failures.

Freezes and closures: the deposit agreement (1 September 2026) lets the bank "suspend or close your Account ... at our discretion with or without notice", and a closed account with a balance above $1.00 is paid out by paper check. In 2026 Relay required customers to reconfirm business details for Thread Bank; accounts not confirmed by 31 August 2026 froze, and after 15 September 2026 they were closed with remaining funds mailed by check. Trustpilot one-star reviews dated 31 July, 17 August and 27 September 2026 report closures without explanation, funds held for an investigation of "up to 45 days", and a payout only by paper check to a US address.

Debit cards run up to 50 per cardholder per checking account with per-card limits and category controls; non-US card transactions cost 1%. The Relay Visa Credit Card is a charge card with a 30-day cycle, no annual fee, a 1% foreign transaction fee and cash back of 1% on Starter, 1.25% on Grow and 1.5% on Scale. 6. Cards, credit & spend controls.research_text:
Both cards are Visa cards issued by Thread Bank. You can issue as many physical and virtual debit cards as you need, up to 50 per cardholder per checking account (pricing page, 17 September 2026), with per-card limits, vendor and category controls, and freeze and terminate controls in the app. Relay charges no ATM fee; Allpoint ATMs carry no operator surcharge and have a $400 per-transaction cap, and non-Allpoint ATMs typically charge around $3.00 per withdrawal. The deposit agreement (1 September 2026) charges 1% on ATM or point-of-sale transactions outside the US; the debit card article says Visa assesses 1 to 2% on non-USD transactions (help articles updated 11 August 2026).

The Relay Visa Credit Card is a charge card: 30-day billing cycle, full balance due at cycle end, 0% periodic rate, no annual fee, late fee up to 3% of the past-due amount, 1% foreign transaction fee (disclosures as of 6 November 2025). Cash back is 1% on Starter, 1.25% on Grow and 1.5% on Scale (17 September 2026), deposited one calendar day after the monthly bill is paid in full; ATM transactions, money orders and cash equivalents do not earn. The limit is cash-based (keep at least $25,000 across Relay accounts) or set by standard underwriting. Eligibility as of 11 August 2026: an LLC, general partnership or corporation, US-incorporated and US-operated, owned by US-based beneficial owners, with either $50,000 or more average monthly revenue over the last 3 months and at least 12 months in business, or $20,000 or more with at least 6 months in business and at least $25,000 held in Relay accounts. No personal or business credit-score check at application; payment activity is reported to major commercial credit bureaus; virtual cards are available; up to five cards per cardholder per credit account. The sources used here do not mention a personal guarantee.

Relay Capital term loans (provided in partnership with Fundbox and its originating bank partner, Lead Bank, per a 20 May 2026 press report) need a valid SSN, a US personal address, a personal credit score of at least 450, at least 3 months of business checking history and annual revenue of $30,000 or more, and carry a fixed fee per draw with no origination fee, repaid by automated weekly ACH (help center, updated 22 May 2026). The sources used here describe no line of credit or venture debt.

7. Payments & international.research_text:
Standard ACH is free on every plan; the next-day cutoff is 10:30 PM EST and delivery takes 1 to 2 business days. Same-day ACH costs $1 on Starter, $0.50 on Grow and nothing on Scale, with a 4:15 PM ET cutoff and no monthly cap on count (updated 11 August 2026). Each account has its own ACH, wire, check and card limits; the exact numbers are set per account and shown in the app rather than published, and increases are approved case by case.

Outgoing domestic wires cost $8 / $5 / $5 by plan, leave in hourly batches from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM EST with a final batch at 5:40 PM, and typically reach the recipient's bank within one business day. SWIFT wires cost $25 / $22 / $20, are typically sent within 2 to 3 business days, and intermediary banks may deduct their own fees. Local Network wires, facilitated by Nium under a program sponsored by Community Federal Savings Bank, cost $5 / $3 / $1.50 (agreement, 1 September 2026) and arrive within three business days in EUR, GBP, CAD or AUD (provider and currency list from a 31 January 2025 post). Non-USD wires carry a conversion fee "as low as 1% depending on the currency and corridor"; rates refresh every 60 seconds and conversion runs Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 6 PM ET. Accounts hold USD only. Inbound international wires arrive in USD, EUR, GBP or CAD and convert to USD automatically; the help center says Relay charges nothing to receive them, while the deposit agreement lists a $5 incoming wire fee.

Paper checks are free to send, are mailed the next business day and typically arrive in 8 to 10 business days; mobile check deposits can take up to 7 business days to settle and checks drawn on non-US banks are not accepted. Zelle is not supported, and the sources used here do not state that RTP or FedNow instant payments are available. Payment approval rules by payment method, initiator, bill attachment, amount, vendor or source account, with one or several approvers, are included on every plan; batched vendor payments and partial payments start on Grow.

8. Integrations & accounting.research_text:
Relay connects directly to QuickBooks Online and Xero for bank feeds and bill pay, and to Hubdoc and Dext for receipt and statement export (help center, updated 11 August 2026). The insured cash sweep is invisible to accounting: monthly statements come from Relay and cover every program bank position together, so QuickBooks Online and Xero connections stay unchanged. Gusto is the direct payroll connection; other payroll providers work by entering the Relay account and routing numbers manually. "Plaid connects Relay to any platform that uses Plaid as its bank-linking service", and Relay lists Airbnb, CashApp, Clover, Melio, PayPal, Shopify, Square, Stripe, Venmo and Wise as payment platforms it works with. Quicken has no direct connection, and YNAB works only if routed through Plaid. The sources used here do not mention NetSuite or Rippling.

There is no API: "Relay does not currently offer a public API" (updated 11 August 2026), so there is no programmatic access beyond the built-in integrations. Sub-accounts are the main structural feature: up to 20 checking accounts on Starter and Grow, 50 on Scale, and 2 savings accounts per business. Users are unlimited on every plan (pricing page, 17 September 2026). Six preset roles (Admin, Manager, Bill Payer, Cardholder, Deposit Only, Read Only) plus custom roles scope access by account; a Read Only user can view transactions, statements and connected integrations but cannot make changes. Accountants are invited as advisors with their own login at Super Admin, Admin, Manager, Bill Payer or Read-only level. Statements export as PDF, CSV or OFX (OFX is web only), with CSV carrying the transaction detail.

9. Lock-in & migration.research_text:
Leaving is cheap but manual. "Relay does not charge you to close your account. There is no closure charge on any subscription plan", but "You cannot close a Relay account from inside the app"; you move the balance out by ACH, wire or check to reach $0, download the statements you want to keep, confirm there are no pending transactions, then contact the Customer Experience team (updated 11 August 2026). After closure "you lose access to the account permanently, including transaction history and any statements you did not download before closing", so export first. Statements export as PDF, CSV or OFX, and bank feeds to QuickBooks Online and Xero keep the history on the accounting side. "Cancelling a paid plan moves you back to the Starter Plan", accounts and integrations stay in place, and "If you downgrade, the unused portion of the higher plan is credited back" (updated 11 August 2026).

Two structural points raise the cost of moving. First, there is no public API, so there is no programmatic export beyond CSV and OFX files. Second, if the bank closes the account, any balance above $1.00 is returned by paper check (deposit agreement, 1 September 2026); a Trustpilot review dated 27 September 2026 describes this as a problem for an owner without physical access to a US address.

Partner bank risk: every account number is a Thread Bank account. The sources used here do not state whether Relay has changed partner banks before or whether account and routing numbers would change if it did, so plan for a possible renumbering and keep payer records current. Up to 50 checking accounts with their own cards also means more payers and subscriptions to repoint when you leave than with a single account.

10. Maturity, trust & support.research_text:
Relay was founded in 2018 in Toronto and remains venture-backed and private: a $32.2 million Series B in May 2024 and $50 million from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund on 19 May 2026, with about 250 staff, more than 150,000 customers and more than $1.3 billion in managed deposits at that date. Relay says it is on track to reach 3.2 times its Series B revenue by the end of 2026, and does not disclose revenue or profitability.

Regulatory record: the sources used here show no public enforcement action against Relay itself. Its partner bank, Thread Bank, received an FDIC consent order on 21 May 2024 over third-party risk management, customer due diligence and AML controls in its banking-as-a-service program; the FDIC terminated that order on 22 December 2025. The sources used here contain no outage history.

Support: Relay's help center offers in-app chat ("Open chat for fast help or to be guided to the right answer") and publishes no hours or response targets. Priority support is included only on Scale (updated 11 August 2026). Relay's Trustpilot company profile lists phone support 9am to 8pm EST, Monday to Friday. Reviews: Trustpilot shows a 4.3 TrustScore from 3,738 reviews as of 5 October 2026, 82% five-star and 11% one-star, with Relay replying to 82% of negative reviews. The one-star cluster is consistent: closures without explanation, funds held for weeks pending investigation, and canned or unhelpful support replies (reviews dated 19 July, 31 July, 17 August, 25 August and 27 September 2026). A four-star review on 5 October 2026 notes support is located overseas.

11. Where it stands out.research_text:
Three concrete advantages. First, account structure at no cost: up to 20 checking accounts on the $0 Starter plan and 50 on Scale, two savings accounts, unlimited users, six preset roles plus custom roles, and advisor logins for accountants, with no monthly fee on Starter and no minimum balance (pricing as of 17 September 2026). Founders who split cash for taxes, payroll and runway get that for free, and the sweep reports as one statement so bookkeeping is unaffected.

Second, low payment costs on the free tier: standard ACH free, same-day ACH $1, outgoing domestic wires $8, SWIFT wires $25, Local Network international wires $5, free paper checks, free cash deposits at Allpoint+ ATMs, and payment approval rules on every plan (deposit agreement 1 September 2026; help center 11 August 2026). Paid tiers bring same-day ACH to $0.50 and then free, and domestic wires to $5.

Third, FDIC coverage without extra products: the IntraFi sweep through Thread Bank covers deposits up to $3,000,000, is automatic, and you keep transacting from Relay as usual (updated 11 August 2026). The charge card adds 1% to 1.5% cash back with no annual fee and a 0% periodic rate (disclosures 6 November 2025), and the 3.21% Scale savings APY (17 September 2026) pays for its $90 monthly fee once average savings pass roughly $53,500.

12. Limitations.text: Founders outside the US face friction: every owner needs a physical US address, the business needs an operating presence in the US, 31 owner countries are prohibited, and one onboarding page demands an SSN for every beneficial owner. Yield is bought with the subscription: Starter savings pay 1.19%, checking pays nothing, and reaching 3.21% costs $90 a month. No public API, no Zelle, no stated RTP or FedNow, and unpublished transaction limits.
12. Limitations.research_text:
Non-US founders face friction. Relay requires a physical US address for every owner with no PO boxes or virtual mailboxes, says the business needs "an operating presence in the U.S.", lists 31 prohibited owner countries, and one onboarding page says "every beneficial owner must have a valid SSN" (all updated 11 August 2026). Closed-account balances above $1.00 go out by paper check (agreement 1 September 2026).

Yield is gated by subscription: Starter savings pay 1.19% APY and no checking APY is listed; reaching 3.21% costs $90 per month, a discounted price that reverts to $120 (17 September 2026). The sources used here describe no treasury or money-market product for larger balances.

No public API and no stated RTP or FedNow support (11 August 2026); Zelle is unsupported; accounts hold USD only; SWIFT wires take 2 to 3 business days to send and non-USD conversion starts at 1%. Transaction limits are set per account and not published.

Credit is thin: the charge card needs $50,000 or more in average monthly revenue with 12 months in business, or $20,000 or more with 6 months in business plus $25,000 held in Relay accounts, and the sources used here describe no line of credit or venture debt.

Counterparty and freeze risk: Thread Bank was under an FDIC consent order from 21 May 2024 to 22 December 2025, the bank may close accounts "with or without notice", and 11% of 3,738 Trustpilot reviews are one-star as of 5 October 2026, with recent one-star reviews describing closures and held funds. Online applications are limited to sole proprietorships, corporations and LLCs managed by a single member or manager with one authorizing representative; a multi-member LLC applies in a branch, where all members (member-managed) or all managers (manager-managed) must be present. Each owner of 10% or more must supply a legal name, residential address, ownership percentage, date of birth, a tax identification number (SSN, ITIN, FTIN or EIN) and country of citizenship. Non-permanent residents can present a passport, matricula or US Employment Authorization Card as primary ID. Chase's general guidance for non-residents, written for personal accounts, says proof of a US address must be provided in the form of a document that shows both your name and address, and that people without an SSN can apply for an ITIN. 5. FDIC coverage & safety.text: Deposits sit directly at JPMorgan Chase Bank with the standard $250,000 of coverage and no sweep on the standard business accounts. The FDIC limit is per depositor, per bank, per ownership category; Chase's own explainer says a corporation's accounts at the bank are combined under the limit, so a C-corp with $1 million in Chase checking and savings has $250,000 insured and $750,000 uninsured. No 2023 or 2024 failure event touched Chase deposits. Chase's Trustpilot profile shows a 1.3 TrustScore from 2,864 reviews, 89% one-star over the prior 12 months (5 October 2026), though it mixes consumer and business complaints.
5. FDIC coverage & safety.research_text: Deposits sit directly at JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., FDIC certificate 628, which the FDIC lists as active and insured since 1934 (data as of 30 June 2026). Coverage is the standard $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category. The fee schedule effective 14 June 2026 says end-of-day sweeps are not permitted with Business Complete Checking, and the sources used here describe no multi-bank sweep program for the standard business accounts. Stocks, bonds, mutual funds, cryptocurrency assets and Treasury bills, bonds or notes are not FDIC covered. 9. Lock-in & migration.research_text: Leaving is manual but there is no stated exit fee: the fee schedule effective 14 June 2026 lists no account closing fee, and Chase's own switch guide tells new customers to close their previous account only after all transactions from it have cleared. Chase is itself the insured bank, so there is no sponsor-bank relationship behind the account that could change hands, which removes one migration risk that applies to accounts run through partner banks. The downside is that leaving means re-pointing every payer and vendor yourself; Chase's switch page lists five steps (set up the account, add funds within 60 days, switch recurring payments and deposits, notify service providers, close the previous account) and provides an Account Switching Guide PDF (no date shown; fetched 5 October 2026). Data portability runs through statements and the third-party data-sharing link, which can be unlinked at any time. Converting to a cash-management product may result in increased fees. Third, scale on the venture side: the J.P. Morgan Innovation Economy practice reports 12,000 clients and 550 or more bankers in 50 or more countries (fetched 5 October 2026), so a company that grows into a priced round has an in-house path to a commercial banker without changing banks.

1. What it is.research_text: Silicon Valley Bank is a chartered bank, not a fintech. Since 27 March 2023 it has operated as a division of First-Citizens Bank & Trust Company, headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina, which bought the failed bank's assets and deposits from the FDIC. Your deposits sit directly at First-Citizens Bank & Trust Company, an FDIC-insured bank; there is no partner-bank layer. The original Silicon Valley Bank was founded in 1983 in San Jose, California, and was closed by the California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation on 10 March 2023. First Citizens announced on 23 April 2026 that it will retire the SVB name in Q4 2026; the technology and healthcare business becomes First Citizens Innovation Banking, and the client FAQ calls this 'a name change, not a change in SVB's go-to-market approach, client service model or solution set'. As of 5 October 2026 svb.com still carries the Silicon Valley Bank name, while firstcitizens.com/innovation already describes the new brand as launched. Scale: SVB reported $108 billion of total client funds and $44 billion of loans for 2025, and its client FAQ says nearly 4,000 clients onboarded 'in the past two years' (undated statement, fetched 5 October 2026). First Citizens' investor deck for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 shows the SVB Commercial segment with $42.5 billion of deposits, $48.1 billion of loans and $80.6 billion of off-balance-sheet client funds at period end; the whole bank held $173.4 billion of deposits and $236.8 billion of assets on that date. 5. FDIC coverage & safety.research_text: Deposits are held directly at First-Citizens Bank & Trust Company, Member FDIC, so standard coverage is $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category (First Citizens acquisition FAQ, fetched 5 October 2026). There is no multi-bank sweep by default; balances above $250,000 in checking or the money market account are uninsured unless you enrol in Insured Cash Sweep, which spreads cash across IntraFi network banks in amounts below $250,000. SVB Cash Sweep money market funds are not deposits and are not FDIC-insured. History matters here. The original Silicon Valley Bank was closed on 10 March 2023; Wikipedia, citing December 2022 regulatory filings, puts more than 85% of its deposits as uninsured, and the FDIC used a systemic risk exception so that 'all depositors of the institution will be made whole' (FDIC, 13 March 2023). First Citizens took over the bridge bank's deposits, about $119 billion as of 10 March 2023, on 27 March 2023, and the FDIC estimated the failure cost its insurance fund about $20 billion. The Federal Reserve's 28 April 2023 review found that SVB's board and management failed to manage their risks and that supervisors 'did not take sufficient steps to ensure that Silicon Valley Bank fixed those problems quickly enough'. None of that applies to the current bank's balance sheet, which reported a preliminary 10.77% CET1 ratio as of 30 June 2026. On freezes, the Deposit Agreement says the bank 'may, at our discretion, and without notice, close, cancel, freeze, suspend or terminate any account'. One Trustpilot review dated 2 November 2025 reports a post-acquisition risk review that reclassified a food-tech business as a money transfer business; the sources used here contain no wider pattern of freeze reports.

6. Cards, credit & spend controls.research_text: Business checking comes with a Mastercard debit card that can be added to a mobile wallet as a digital card. Foreign debit transactions carry a 2.00% International Service Assessment (fee schedule, fetched 5 October 2026). The credit product for early-stage and Series A startups is the SVB Innovator Card, a charge card issued by First-Citizens Bank & Trust Company on the Mastercard network: the statement balance is due in full each cycle and there is no right to carry a balance. SVB markets it with 'higher credit limits with no personal liability'. The terms revised May 2026 list a $0 annual membership fee, a foreign currency transaction fee of 0 to 3% of the amount, a late payment fee of the greater of $32 or 2.5% of the statement balance, a $29 returned payment fee and a cash advance fee of 3% (minimum $3, maximum $50). Rewards are 1.5X points on all Innovator Card spend with no caps, redeemable as statement credit; virtual cards earn 1X. A sign-up offer running to 31 December 2026 pays 250,000 points for $60,000 of spend in the first 90 days, or 45,000 points for $10,000. The card page says you can manage card spend for employee stipends, travel, procurement and payables, and the travel and expense platform is included at no extra cost. The Accelerator Card, aimed at high-growth venture-funded companies, pays cash rebates and is the product SVB describes with instant virtual card issuance with custom limits, spend policies and categories. With 10 or more Innovator cards outstanding the company is liable for all charges, including unauthorized use, apart from skimmed or counterfeited cards. The sources used here do not state how credit limits are sized for pre-revenue companies. SVB's venture debt article describes loans typically sized at 25 to 35% of the last equity round, with a 6 to 12 month interest-only period and repayment within three to four years, all subject to underwriting.

11. Where it stands out.research_text: Three things are concrete. First, a chartered bank with a startup product: deposits are held directly at an FDIC-insured bank with $236.8 billion of assets as of 30 June 2026, and the Startup Money Market Account pays 3.56% APY above $1 million and 2.63% between $50,000.01 and $1 million as of 30 September 2026, with Insured Cash Sweep available for multimillion-dollar FDIC coverage. Second, wires are bundled for an early team: Essentials includes 15 outgoing wires a month at no charge, including 5 international FX wires, and incoming wires cost $10 after the bundle, with the $25 monthly fee waived above a $15,000 average balance (as of 5 October 2026). Third, credit and lending are in-house: the Innovator Card is a $0 annual fee charge card marketed with 'no personal liability' and 1.5X rewards with no caps (terms revised May 2026), and the same bank writes venture debt, which its own article sizes at 25 to 35% of the last round, with $44 billion of loans on its books for 2025. The payment rails are also documented: same-day ACH to $1 million, next-day ACH to $99.9 million and RTP transfers to $10 million, with up to two approvers per payment and a published API (as of 5 October 2026). The client FAQ confirms service to non-US clients on a cross-border basis, which matters for founders abroad with a US entity.

Limitations.research_text: Onboarding is a sales process: you submit a form and wait for a team member, credit products need underwriting approval, and SVB publishes no time-to-open (as of 5 October 2026). The bank's current public pages do not state SSN, ITIN, address or entity rules; the only document that does is a 2021 Global Gateway sheet from before the First Citizens purchase. Standard FDIC coverage is $250,000 unless you enrol in Insured Cash Sweep, and the sweep yields and fees are not published. Costs stack once you grow past the Essentials bundle: $32 standard maintenance, $0.15 per ACH, $40 a month for online ACH service, $25 per international wire, a 2% fee on foreign debit card spend and 0 to 3% on foreign Innovator Card spend, and $30 per daily overdraft up to $150 a day (fee schedule, fetched 5 October 2026). Cash deposits have no published route since SVB accounts are not serviced in First Citizens branches. Support is business hours only, 5:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Pacific on weekdays, and Trustpilot rates the bank 2.0 of 5 on 12 reviews as of 2 November 2025. The Deposit Agreement allows closure or freeze without notice. Finally, the name goes away in Q4 2026; nothing changes operationally according to First Citizens, and the sources used here do not say whether account or routing numbers change.

1. What it is.research_text: The internal build is not a product. You open a plain business checking account at an FDIC-insured bank or credit union, then do by hand what the fintech accounts bundle. Coverage is the FDIC's standard $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category (FDIC page last updated 1 April 2024), and a corporation's deposits at one bank are combined under that single cap (FDIC brochure updated 14 May 2024). To insure more, you open accounts at more banks yourself, or ask your bank for IntraFi's ICS or CDARS, which place funds in increments that do not exceed the FDIC maximum at other network banks; IntraFi says 91 of the top 100 US banks and 64% of US banks participate (fetched 5 October 2026). 2. Eligibility & onboarding.research_text: Any US entity with an EIN can apply. The SBA lists an EIN (or SSN for a sole proprietorship), formation documents, ownership agreements and a business license as the usual paperwork (fetched 5 October 2026). Each bank adds its own rules. Bank of America states "Applicants should be US residents" and "Foreign business customers are unable to apply at this time", and asks for an SSN and date of birth for everyone on the application, including every owner at 25% or more and the controlling manager; corporations can apply online (fetched 5 October 2026). Wells Fargo requires a physical address: "Registered Agents, Virtual Addresses, and PO/Commercial mailboxes are not acceptable"; it accepts a passport as primary ID and prefers all owners present at opening, with notarized forms for absent owners (fetched 5 October 2026). One big bank opens accounts online only if the business is "a sole proprietorship, corporation, or an LLC managed by a single member or manager"; any other structure applies at a branch, and two forms of personal ID are required (fetched 5 October 2026). Minimum opening deposits are $25 at Wells Fargo (schedule effective 28 July 2026) and $0 at Bank of America (fetched 5 October 2026). Credit unions add a membership step: Navy Federal requires the owners to be members first (fetched 5 October 2026). A TreasuryDirect entity account is open to corporations, LLCs, partnerships and sole proprietorships; the entity's TIN is required and the entity and its account manager must certify they are US persons (fetched 5 October 2026). 5. FDIC coverage & safety.text: Coverage is the FDIC's standard $250,000 per depositor at each insured bank. A corporation's deposits at one bank are combined under that cap however many owners sign, and each extra bank carries its own $250,000, which is why splitting works; IntraFi's ICS and CDARS do the splitting through one bank, with depositor fees its pages do not publish. The March 2023 bank failure showed both the limit and the discretion in the deposit route: the FDIC made all depositors whole under a systemic risk exception, a discretionary act, not a rule.
5. FDIC coverage & safety.research_text: Coverage is the standard $250,000 per depositor, per FDIC-insured bank, per ownership category (FDIC page updated 1 April 2024). A corporation's deposits at one bank are "combined and insured up to $250,000", and the number of owners or signatories does not raise it (FDIC brochure updated 14 May 2024). Splitting cash across banks works because each bank carries its own $250,000; the FDIC's own example says a depositor is insured "at each FDIC-insured bank". IntraFi's ICS and CDARS do the splitting through one bank, with BNY Mellon as sub-custodian; IntraFi's pages do not publish depositor fees (fetched 5 October 2026). Nothing you buy for yield is FDIC-insured: the FDIC lists mutual funds, stocks, bonds and U.S. Treasury bills, bonds or notes as not covered (page updated 1 April 2024). A brokerage account carries SIPC protection of $500,000 including $250,000 for cash, and money market funds count as protected securities (fetched 5 October 2026). The 2023 failures showed the deposit route's floor and its ceiling: when a venture-focused bank failed in March 2023 the FDIC made all depositors whole on 13 March 2023 under a systemic risk exception, which is a discretionary act, not a rule. The 2024 consent orders against banking-as-a-service banks (Blue Ridge, Lineage, Sutton, Piermont, Mode Eleven, Thread, Evolve) hit the partner-bank model, not direct deposits (Banking Dive, 18 December 2024; the Federal Reserve's Evolve action is dated 14 June 2024). A bill to insure noninterest-bearing business accounts to $10,000,000 (S. 2999) was introduced 9 October 2025 and is not law. The sources used here do not report freeze or closure patterns for plain big-bank business accounts.

6. Cards, credit & spend controls.text: The deposit accounts come with a business debit card and employee debit cards and nothing else. There is no charge card, no cashback and no virtual cards; business credit cards and lines of credit are separate applications whose terms the sources used here do not state. Bank of America's employee debit cards default to a $400 daily purchase limit, adjustable to $7,500; Wells Fargo lets you adjust daily limits and turn a card on or off. That is the whole control surface: a daily cap and a switch, with no category blocks, merchant locks or receipt matching.
6. Cards, credit & spend controls.research_text: You get the bank's business debit card and whatever employee cards it issues; there is no charge card, no cashback program and no virtual card in the sources used here. Bank of America issues employee debit cards at an owner's request and lets the owner "set and modify debit card spending limits for employees"; the purchase limit defaults to $400 a day, adjustable to a maximum of $7,500, and the ATM limit defaults to $100, adjustable to $700; cards can be locked in the app (fetched 5 October 2026). Wells Fargo issues a business deposit card to employees who are not signers, lets you adjust daily purchase and ATM limits, and lets you turn a card on or off; it tells you the limit amounts when the card arrives rather than publishing them (fetched 5 October 2026). That is the whole control surface on these pages: a per-card daily cap and an on/off switch. The bank pages used here describe no category blocks, merchant locks, per-vendor virtual cards or receipt matching; you enforce policy by reading statements and asking for receipts. Foreign-currency card purchases cost 3% at Wells Fargo (schedule effective 28 July 2026) and 3% at Bank of America (schedule effective 20 February 2026). Business credit cards and lines of credit are separate applications at each bank, and the sources used here do not state their approval rules, limits or whether a personal guarantee is required. Venture debt is not part of this route.

7. Payments & international.research_text: Wires are the expensive part. Wells Fargo charges $30 for a digital outgoing domestic wire, $30 for a digital outgoing international wire in US dollars, $40 for any wire sent in a branch, and nothing for incoming wires on non-analyzed accounts; its Navigate tier ($25 a month) includes the first two outgoing domestic wires per fee period (schedule effective 28 July 2026). Bank of America charges $30 outgoing domestic, $15 incoming domestic, $45 outgoing international in US dollars and $15 incoming international (schedule effective 20 February 2026). Both banks send foreign-currency wires with no wire fee and earn on the exchange rate instead: Wells Fargo's schedule says "Wells Fargo makes money when it converts one currency to another for you" and that its rate "includes a markup"; Bank of America's says "exchange rate markups apply". Neither publishes the margin. Ten outbound wires a month at $30 to $45 is $300 to $450. The free transaction allowances count differently: Wells Fargo counts all checks deposited and all withdrawals or debits, paper and electronic, except debit card purchases and payments, against Initiate's 100 free items; Bank of America exempts debit card transactions and electronic debits from Fundamentals' 20 free items, so checks paid and other non-electronic debits are what count. Wells Fargo prices same-day ACH at $1.50 per item only on its analyzed accounts, and the sources used here do not state ACH limits or same-day ACH availability for the entry-level accounts. The sources used here do not state whether RTP or FedNow instant payments are offered on these accounts, and do not describe multi-step payment approvals for entry-level accounts.

8. Integrations & accounting.text: The bank feed is the integration. Xero pulls transactions daily and names Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Capital One and Citibank among its direct feeds; QuickBooks says bank and card transactions sync automatically. Stripe and payroll providers pay in by ACH like anyone else, and there is no API, no webhooks and no programmatic access on the deposit side. Reconciliation is not automatic: both products describe the feed as automatic, but matching it to statements each month is still a manual task.

9. Lock-in & migration.text: Lock-in is low in structure and high in labor. Your account numbers belong to the bank you chose, so they never change because a software vendor swapped partner banks; they change only if you change banks, when every payroll run, Stripe payout and vendor autopay must be re-pointed by hand. Neither the Wells Fargo nor the Bank of America schedule lists a closure fee, and Bank of America charges no monthly fee in the first year, so a first-year exit costs nothing. Treasury bills bought at TreasuryDirect can be moved to a broker to sell early, normally for a fee; holding to maturity avoids it.
9. Lock-in & migration.research_text: Lock-in is low in structure and high in labor. Your account numbers belong to the bank you chose, so they do not change when a software vendor swaps partner banks; they change only if you change banks, at which point every payroll run, Stripe payout and vendor autopay must be re-pointed by hand. The Wells Fargo schedule effective 28 July 2026 and the Bank of America schedule effective 20 February 2026 list no account closure fee. Bank of America does not assess its $16 monthly fee until the thirteenth statement cycle closes, so a first-year exit costs nothing in monthly fees. Data portability is statements and bank feeds: QuickBooks and Xero pull transactions from the bank directly, so switching accounting software does not touch the bank. Treasury bills bought at TreasuryDirect can be moved to a broker to sell early, but "normally there is a fee for this service" at the receiving broker (TreasuryDirect FAQ, fetched 5 October 2026); holding to maturity avoids it, and bills run 4 to 52 weeks. CDARS placements are CDs with maturities of 4 weeks to 3 years, so an early exit depends on the terms your bank set (fetched 5 October 2026). Spreadsheets, card policy and budgets are yours and move with you. The sources used here do not state export formats for the bank portals beyond statements and feeds.

10. Maturity, trust & support.research_text: The institutions are old and regulated; the route itself has no vendor. Deposits sit at chartered banks under FDIC rules on pages last revised 1 April 2024 and 14 May 2024. Regulator history matters when you pick the bank: the Federal Reserve lifted the 2018 asset growth restriction on Wells Fargo on 3 June 2025, saying the bank "has fulfilled the conditions required for removal of the growth restriction" while "the other provisions in the 2018 enforcement action will remain in place"; the 2024 consent orders against Blue Ridge, Lineage, Sutton, Piermont, Mode Eleven, Thread and Evolve were aimed at banking-as-a-service banks, which this route avoids (Banking Dive, 18 December 2024; the Federal Reserve's Evolve action is dated 14 June 2024). When a venture-focused bank failed in March 2023 the FDIC said "All depositors of the institution will be made whole" (13 March 2023). Support runs through the bank's branches and phone lines; the sources used here do not measure response times. Public review scores for the big banks are poor and mostly retail: Trustpilot shows Bank of America at 1.4 from 3,665 reviews, Wells Fargo at 1.2 from 1,608, and a third big bank at 1.3 from 2,864 (all fetched 5 October 2026). Hacker News commenters in March 2023 described spreading cash across banks as "regularly done" (10 March 2023), and a reply to a commenter who spreads personal funds across banks called it "quite the hassle" (12 March 2023). TreasuryDirect, IntraFi, QuickBooks and Xero are all established services, but no one is accountable for the combination; that is you.
