11. Where it stands out.text:
No platform layer sits between you and the insured bank. Coverage is the FDIC's own $250,000 per depositor per bank, and Treasury bills bought at TreasuryDirect carry no management fee.
The 2024 consent orders that hit banking-as-a-service banks do not touch a deposit held directly at a chartered bank. The 13-week Treasury bill auction of 5 October 2026 cleared at 4.149%, against 3.69% on the Crane 100 money fund index. Running cost is near zero at low balances: Wells Fargo Initiate is $0 with a $2,000 balance, Bank of America Fundamentals charges nothing in the first year, and Navy Federal Business Checking has no monthly fee.
11. Where it stands out.research_text: Three concrete advantages. First, no platform layer between you and the insured bank: coverage is the FDIC's own $250,000 per depositor per bank (page updated 1 April 2024), and the 2024 consent orders that hit seven banking-as-a-service banks (Banking Dive, 18 December 2024) do not touch a deposit held directly at a chartered bank. Second, yield at the source with no management fee: the 13-week Treasury bill auction of 5 October 2026 cleared at 4.149% and the 4-week auction of 1 October 2026 at 3.956%, bought with no fee at TreasuryDirect or for $0 online at Fidelity (both fetched 5 October 2026), against a 3.69% seven-day yield on the Crane 100 money fund index as of 5 October 2026. Third, near-zero running cost at low balances: Wells Fargo Initiate is $0 with a $2,000 minimum daily balance (schedule effective 28 July 2026), Bank of America Fundamentals is not assessed until the thirteenth statement cycle closes and is then $0 with $500 of net debit purchases in a cycle (schedule effective 20 February 2026), Navy Federal Business Checking has no monthly fee (fetched 5 October 2026), and Western Alliance waives monthly maintenance, online wire, mobile deposit and ACH fees for three years or until institutional funding (fetched 5 October 2026). A fourth, softer advantage is a branch: Wells Fargo prefers all owners present at opening and takes notarized forms from any who are not, and one big bank opens accounts for structures beyond a sole proprietorship, a corporation or an LLC managed by a single member or manager only at a branch (both fetched 5 October 2026).

Limitations.text: Coverage stops at $250,000 per bank for the whole corporation; every dollar above that needs another bank, another login and another feed, or an IntraFi placement whose cost is not published. Wires cost $30 to $45 each at Wells Fargo and Bank of America, and foreign-currency wires carry an unpublished exchange markup. 12. Limitations.research_text: The drawbacks are concrete. Coverage stops at $250,000 per bank for the whole corporation (FDIC brochure, 14 May 2024); every dollar above that needs another bank, another login, another feed, or an IntraFi placement whose cost the IntraFi pages do not publish (fetched 5 October 2026). Wires cost $30 to $45 each at Wells Fargo and Bank of America (schedules effective 28 July 2026 and 20 February 2026), and foreign-currency wires carry an unpublished exchange markup. Spend control is a daily cap and an on/off switch; Bank of America's employee card tops out at $7,500 a day and its page describes no merchant or category rules (fetched 5 October 2026). Founders outside the US are blocked: Bank of America says "Foreign business customers are unable to apply at this time" and Wells Fargo rejects registered-agent and virtual addresses (both fetched 5 October 2026). At one big bank, only a sole proprietorship, a corporation or an LLC managed by a single member or manager can open online; any other structure applies at a branch (fetched 5 October 2026). Entry-level checking pays 0% to 0.01% (Wells Fargo and Bank of America 2026 schedules; Navy Federal Business Checking, fetched 5 October 2026), so idle cash earns nothing until you move it. Reconciliation is manual and fragile: "the bank feed will just silently drop transactions" (Hacker News, 19 April 2019). Selling a Treasury bill early means transferring it to a broker, where "normally there is a fee for this service" (TreasuryDirect, fetched 5 October 2026). Big-bank Trustpilot scores sit at 1.2 to 1.4 (fetched 5 October 2026). The sources used here do not quantify the hours this route takes each month.
